models.purpose: Cover a country with the fewest charging stations at least cost.
models.summary: Vehicle density is population density times 0.77 cars per person. Honeycomb cells cover each region so overlap is smallest. Along interstates a fast charger sits every 50 miles on 3,951,098 miles of main road, giving 0.08 million rural superchargers. The US total is 6.55 million stations: 2.23 urban, 3.00 suburban, 1.28 rural, of which 5.56 million are destination chargers. Ireland, treated as two regions, needs 87.70 thousand.

governing_equations.purpose: one fast charger per fifty miles of main road

objectives: Cover a country with the fewest charging stations at least cost.
constraints: cells may not overlap more than the honeycomb forces

parameter_estimation.method: ownership 0.77 from the cited census figure, road length from the cited highway list

assumptions: distance is the straight line between two points
vehicles of one class are spread evenly

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: US total of 6.55 million matches the sum of the three regions

validation_refs: station counts checked against the summary totals
strengths: the same coverage rule is reused for a second country
limitations: table 4.1 totals 6.47 million inside states while the summary and table 4.3 say 6.55
missing_details: the fitted coefficients of the growth curve are not printed

models.purpose: Order construction by a single urgency index.
models.summary: Service capacity, population density and wealth are normalized and combined into one urgency score, and stations are built from the most urgent down. At 30 percent coverage Ireland has 26.31 thousand stations, at 50 percent 43.85 thousand, at full coverage 87.70 thousand. A cost term is added later, and the country-level index AI decides the order: below 0.2 rural first, above 0.65 urban first, otherwise both.

variables.definition: vehicles served per unit area, normalized
country index comparing urban and rural urgency

governing_equations.source_expression: order = rural if AI<0.2, urban if AI>0.65, else both
governing_equations.purpose: construction order from two cutoffs on the priority index

objectives: Order construction by a single urgency index.

parameter_estimation.method: weights described as equal after normalization, not fitted

assumptions: a more urgent station is always built before a less urgent one

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: the ordering is tabulated for Ireland but the weights are not estimated

validation_refs: station counts checked against the summary totals
strengths: the same coverage rule is reused for a second country
limitations: the cost formula is printed with missing symbols, so the optimized index cannot be recomputed
missing_details: the fitted coefficients of the growth curve are not printed

models.purpose: Date Ireland's full coverage from a US growth curve rescaled by two ratios.
models.summary: US electric-vehicle growth from 2005 to 2016 is fit by a logistic curve. Ireland is the same curve with coefficients scaled by two ratios: US population density is 0.5 of Ireland's and US GDP per capita is 0.93 of Ireland's. The rescaled curve reaches full coverage in about 18.1 years. The handout quotes a world average of about 163 years, which is not derived in the body.

variables.definition: US population density divided by Ireland's, printed as 0.5
US GDP per capita divided by Ireland's, printed as 0.93
years until electric vehicles cover the fleet

governing_equations.source_expression: years_Ireland = logistic(US data, scaled by 0.5 and 0.93)

constraints: vehicle ownership in Ireland is treated as fixed
